text: Coccidiosis in cattle usually affects young animals from about 3 weeks to 6 months old, occasionally up to 2 years. Signs: diarrhea with chronic weight loss/wasting; in severe cases, blood and mucus in the manure, sticky black manure soiling the tail and hindquarters, and straining during defecation. Treatment: Sulfadimidine (Sulfa 33) by injection or orally, or Amprolium at 10 mg/kg/day for 5 days. Prevention: Amprolium at 5 mg/kg/day for 21 days.
